looks.title: Canyon from a viewpoint
looks.credit: Grand Canyon view from Pima Point, Chensiyuan, CC BY-SA 4.0, Wikimedia Commons
looks.summary: A sweeping view into the Grand Canyon, with the muddy Colorado River winding through the inner gorge beneath layered red rock buttes under a cloudy sky.

claims.label: Colorado River
claims.claim: The muddy, reddish-brown Colorado River curves through the bottom of the inner gorge.
claims.spot: Follow the winding brown ribbon of water near the bottom-center of the frame.
claims.know: The Colorado River carved the Grand Canyon to a depth of over a mile over roughly 5-6 million years.

claims.label: Sunlit canyon buttes
claims.claim: Warm, sunlit ridges and buttes of layered sedimentary rock rise on the right side of the gorge.
claims.spot: The brightest orange and tan rock faces, catching low-angle sunlight on the right.
claims.know: The distinct bands are limestone, sandstone, and shale layers deposited over hundreds of millions of years.

claims.label: Cloudy sky
claims.claim: A gray, overcast sky filled with layered clouds hangs above the far canyon rim.
claims.spot: The upper third of the photo, above the hazy horizon of distant plateaus.
claims.know: Grand Canyon's elevation of about 7,000 feet on the rim makes weather there markedly cooler than the river below.

claims.label: Shadowed green slope
claims.claim: A broad slope in shadow, dotted with muted green desert vegetation, fills the left-middle of the view.
claims.spot: The dark, low-contrast hillside with sparse green-gray shrubs on the left.
claims.know: Vegetation there includes pinyon pine and juniper, which survive on limited rainfall of around 10-15 inches per year.

claims.label: Inner plateau
claims.claim: A sunlit, flattish plateau cut by side drainages sits in the middle of the canyon between the rims.
claims.spot: The pale, striated terrace in the center with visible erosion channels.
claims.know: Such benches are formed by resistant rock layers, like the Bright Angel Shale, that erode more slowly than rock above and below.

looks.title: Kitchen utensils on a rail
looks.credit: Kitchen utensils, Darren Lewis, CC0, Wikimedia Commons
looks.summary: A close-up of assorted kitchen utensils—including a whisk, grater, spatulas, and a slicer—hanging on hooks against a white tiled wall.

claims.label: Wire whisk
claims.claim: A chrome balloon whisk with many thin wires hangs prominently in the center of the photo.
claims.spot: Cluster of shiny looped wires with a black ring where they meet the handle.
claims.know: Its wires are designed to whip air into egg whites or cream for meringues and mousses.

claims.label: Box grater
claims.claim: A stainless steel box grater with punched shredding holes stands on the right side.
claims.spot: Tall rectangular metal panel with rows of raised grating teeth.
claims.know: Standard box graters have four sides with different coarseness levels, from zesting to slicing.
claims.humanNote: a flat grater rather than a box grater, but a grater is there

claims.label: Slotted spatula
claims.claim: A black slotted turner with long parallel openings hangs diagonally down the middle-left.
claims.spot: Wide black plastic blade with lengthwise slots running down its face.
claims.know: The slots let hot grease or water drain away so food stays crisp.
claims.humanNote: only the black handle is in this cell; the slotted head is lower down

claims.label: Skimmer spoon
claims.claim: A black skimmer spoon with round draining holes shows at the lower left.
claims.spot: Bowl-shaped head pierced with several large circular holes.
claims.know: Skimmers are used to lift food from boiling water or to skim foam from stocks and jams.
claims.humanNote: the perforated black skimmer fills the crop

claims.label: V-slicer mandoline
claims.claim: A metal mandoline slicer with a V-shaped blade and gripping teeth hangs at the top right.
claims.spot: Shiny steel surface with vertical slit blades and a round safety-grip piece.
claims.know: Mandolines can be adjusted for paper-thin slices or julienne cuts, but cause many kitchen cuts.
claims.humanNote: a metal wire slicer, not a mandoline

claims.label: Ladle
claims.claim: The deep black bowl of a ladle peeks out at the bottom center-right below the whisk.
claims.spot: Rounded cup-shaped scooping end behind the whisk wires.
claims.know: Ladles are sized by milliliters so servings of soup or sauce are consistent.
claims.humanNote: the black ladle bowl is at the bottom of the crop

looks.title: Cat on a wall
looks.credit: Cat November 2010-1a, Alvesgaspar, CC BY-SA 3.0, Wikimedia Commons
looks.summary: A tabby cat with green eyes sits alertly on a whitewashed stone wall against a blurred backdrop of bare branches and blue sky.

claims.label: Green-eyed cat face
claims.claim: The cat's head faces the camera squarely, with pale green eyes, perked ears, and an orange-pink nose.
claims.spot: Centered in the top-middle cell between the two grid lines crossing the ears and nose.
claims.know: The green eye color comes from low melanin in the iris, a trait more common in cats with mackerel tabby coats.

claims.label: White muzzle and whiskers
claims.claim: Bright white fur on the chin and muzzle stands out beneath the nose, with long white whiskers sweeping outward.
claims.spot: Just below the nose at the middle-left intersection of the grid.
claims.know: Whiskers are rooted three times deeper than regular fur and are roughly as sensitive as a human's fingertips.

claims.label: Front paws on wall
claims.claim: The cat's striped forelegs stretch straight down, with both front paws planted on the rough white ledge.
claims.spot: Bottom-middle-left cell where the legs meet the pale stone at the photo's bottom edge.
claims.know: Cats are digitigrade, meaning they walk on their toe bones rather than the flats of their feet.

claims.label: Striped tabby haunches
claims.claim: The seated hindquarters fill the lower-right of the body, showing dense dark stripes over brownish fur.
claims.spot: Lower-center-right cell with the darkest, most tightly banded fur on the cat.
claims.know: Tabby is a coat pattern, not a breed, and every tabby's stripe layout is unique like a fingerprint.

claims.label: Bare branches and sky
claims.claim: Thin leafless twigs crisscross a soft blue sky, heavily blurred in the upper-left background.
claims.spot: Top-left cell, everywhere the cat is not, with gray branching lines over blue.
claims.know: The blur comes from a shallow depth of field, meaning the camera used a wide lens aperture focused close up.

check.seen: Cat beside bare branches and sky

human: Each claim was checked against its crop by a person (the app author) after recording.
